correctness.rationale: Write a general map as R(1)=a1+u and R(v)=f(v)1+T(v). Evaluating weight-zero Rota-Baxter on (v,w) forces f(v)f(w)=2f(v)f(w), hence f=0 in every char; evaluating (1,1) forces a=0 and 2T(u)=0; (1,v) forces T^2=0. Conversely RHS terms reduce to 2stT(u)+tT²(v)+sT²(w)=0, matching LHS. R²(1)=T(u), R²(v)=0, so exponent sharp. For rank r image E<=ker H of dim n-r choose E and H and isomorphism V/H to E gives N_r=[n r]_q[n-r r]_q|GL(r,q)|. Rank R is r if u in E else r+1; allowed u=all V char2, kerT otherwise; yields polynomial. A centralizer of fixed Jordan type acts transitively on 0,E�,(kerT)\E, V\kerT, giving four orbit counts, last allowed only char2. Independent full-matrix tests (not parametrization-only) for (n,q)=(1,2),(1,3),(2,2),(2,3),(3,2) reproduced n2q2 total16, R²!=0 count6; n2q3 total33; n3q2 total176, R²!=0 count84 and their rank distributions. General theorem rests on structural proof, finite tests are only independent checks.

value.rationale: Rota-Baxter operator classification is a natural algebraic problem; the characteristic-two jump of sharp nilpotency index is a structurally motivated boundary absent in characteristic zero. The complete finite-field rank generating polynomial and GL(V)-orbit stratification make the classification usable across all n and q, beyond a routine small-table recomputation.
residual_risks: No claims for nonzero weights, nonsplit residue-field extensions or higher radical powers.

final_claim: On A=K1+V with V^2=0 and dim_K V=n>=1 over any field, every weight-zero Rota-Baxter operator is uniquely R(a1+v)=a u+T(v), with T^2=0 and 2T(u)=0. Thus R^2=0 for characteristic not two; in characteristic two R^3=0 and R^2 can be nonzero iff n>=2. Over finite fields the stated Gaussian-binomial N_r counts yield exact linear-rank polynomial and four natural GL(V)-orbit types (last occurs only in characteristic two).
limitations: Characteristic-zero operator classification is known and is explicitly credited
Arbitrary characteristic classification proved algebraically; finite verification limited to sample prime fields
Nonzero RB weight, nonsplit local rings and radical cubics outside scope.
